The most material change is the sharp decline in the latest top-100 breadth proxy (44 advancers versus 69 in the prior capture), alongside negative 24h/72h BTC and ETH returns and negative longer-window aggressive quote flow. This is a deterioration signal, but not a confirmed distribution phase: the captures use rolling windows and changed point-in-time membership, the separate rich-breadth proxy is not canonical, and positive short-interval marks, persistent ETH/BTC closes above 0.03, and positive 30d/90d relative-alt context argue against a clean, one-way breakdown. The mixed cross-horizon evidence is more consistent with stalled/fragile conditions than confirmed continuation or persistent late-cycle deterioration. A short-term pause or failed transition cannot be distinguished reliably from renewed strength. Current data cannot resolve the risk of interpreting a temporary pullback as a reason to exit too early, nor the risk of waiting too long if breadth and leadership weakness persists. The one-hour sequence is unavailable and temporal coherence records an existing anchor-tolerance violation; ranges above are shadow research candidates only.
